title: Ají Verde (Peruvian Green Sauce)

items.name: fresh cilantro, packed, thin stems included
items.amount: 1 cup (about ⅔ of a large bunch)

items.name: kosher salt
items.amount: ⅛ teaspoon, plus more to taste

steps: Rinse the cilantro, picking out any yellow or slimy leaves and the thick lower stems. The thin upper stems can stay. Shake it as dry as you can; water left on the leaves thins the sauce.

Put the wet ingredients in the blender first: lime juice, olive oil, and the yogurt or mayonnaise. Add the queso fresco, jalapeño if using, garlic, green onion, salt, and pepper, then pack the cilantro in on top.
Blend for 1–2 minutes, stopping to scrape down the sides, until it's completely smooth and evenly green. It looks grainy at first; keep going.
Taste and adjust with more salt, lime, or jalapeño. It should taste slightly salty on its own. If it's too thick, loosen it with a little more lime juice or a splash of water.
If there's time, chill it for 30 minutes so the raw garlic softens. A squeeze bottle makes it easy to drizzle.
notes: Greek yogurt makes it tangier than mayonnaise does, so add the lime a little at a time. Without the jalapeño it's a mild, herby sauce; with it, start with ½ and add more after tasting. Chives work in place of the green onion. Feta works in place of the queso fresco; it's saltier, so hold the salt until you taste. Halves easily in a small blender cup. Good over rice bowls, roasted potatoes, tacos, or eggs. Protein: about 14g per batch with Greek yogurt (yogurt ~6g, queso fresco ~8g), so about 3–4g per ¼ cup. With mayonnaise, about 8g per batch.
freezeNote: Doesn't freeze: the dairy turns grainy and the cilantro dulls. It's brightest the day it's made, so make what gets eaten.
